<reason>PRO won a close, high-quality clash by making the live comparison easier to vote on: unpaid non-educational placements as a family-income filter, not an open first rung. CON landed real blows—conversion largely failed, PRO admitted typical deletion, and the educational line is messy—but never cleanly answered the wage-floor stopping-point or showed that the typical contested slot was actually usable by the unconnected. PRO’s honest “often a deleted slot” plus “she could not take that slot” reframing, and the “only makes sense unpaid” crystallization, outweighed CON’s ash-and-nephew second-order story.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO’s R1 dilemma (valued labour is already a sham; genuine teaching is carved out) and the later turn of CON’s “only makes sense if cash is not required” into a means-test indictment, which CON never fully unpicked.</best_rebuttal>
